messages:
rachel: Noticed host p95 blowup on small HTTP/2 requests after kernel-selector tweak. Affects seq <= 100.

dmitri: Saw that too. Baseline perf: p95 ~14ms, after change ~28ms. Flamegraph shows majority in header parsing and lots of tiny socket writes.

jas: Rat hole looks like: tokenization -> header_parse -> write_small_frames -> sys_writev. Also kv::auth_lookup appears intermittently adding jitter.

olga: Did kernel selector change disable intra-host microbatching? I recall it prefers 'latency' kernels which avoid batching timers.

dmitri: Exactly. For short sequences we route to low-latency kernel which bypasses the batching queue. That reduces throughput but increases syscall churn for many concurrent small requests.

rachel: Quick pprof top:
pprof -top host_smallframe.prof
  37%  header::parse_headers
  26%  transport::write_small_frames
  11%  net::writev_syscall
  7%   kv::lookup_cold
  4%   alloc::malloc

jas: Short mitigations to try: (1) coalesce small frame writes in transport, (2) use pooled buffers for header parsing to cut mallocs, (3) prepopulate auth keys in KV on hot hosts.

olga: I landed a tiny transport coalesce behind flag (batch up to 8KB or 2ms). Canary on rdx-host-12 shows p95 down from 28ms -> 16.5ms on small-http2 workload.

dmitri: Good! With pooled header buffers and KV prewarm on that host p95 further drops to ~12.8ms. Kernel-selector still matters: if we allow microbatching for seq<=100 with a 1ms micro-wait, p95 goes to 9.6ms but p50 rises slightly.

rachel: Action items: roll transport_coalesce to 20% then 100% (ticket INF-732), implement header buffer pool (INF-733), script kernel-selector perf sweep (INF-734). Coordinate with SRE for canary windows.

perf-bot: Canary deploy 3934567891 by olga started on rdx-host-12. Artifacts: /perf/3934567890/coalesce-canary.tar.gz

jas: We'll also run matrix across seq lengths [8,32,64,128] and batch sizes [1,4,8] and measure KV hot/cold conditions. Expect kernel selection to change tradeoffs.

rachel: Thanks all — keeping thread as single place for results.
